title.narrative: Emergency Response to Flood-Affected Communities in Adamawa State, Nigeria

description.narrative: The project seeks to deliver life-saving emergency assistance to approximately 10,000 individuals (1,667 households) severely impacted by recent flooding in Yola. This crisis was validated through a rapid needs assessment conducted in collaboration with local authorities, community leaders, and humanitarian agencies, ensuring an accurate understanding of the immediate impacts. Critically, affected families actively participated in focus group discussions and community mapping sessions, openly sharing their priorities and challenges. Their insights have directly shaped the intervention’s design, prioritizing shelter, access to safe water, improved sanitation, and essential protection services that respond to the needs they identified. Key Priority Needs Identified: • Emergency Shelter materials for displaced families. • Non-Food Items (NFIs), including blankets, mats, cooking utensils, and lighting. • Health and WASH Support: Trauma kits, cholera kits, water purification tablets, hygiene kits, and essential medicines. This project’s approach is intentionally structured to respond directly and comprehensively to emergency shelter materials, essential non-food items, health and WASH assistance, which has been tailored to address the specific challenges articulated by affected households and community members. Health and WASH support, including trauma kits, cholera kits, water purification tablets, hygiene supplies, and essential medicines—responds to the acute risk of disease outbreaks and deteriorating sanitary conditions, while the focus on mental health and psychosocial support targets the trauma and stress resulting from the flooding, offering pathways to healing and recovery.
